item.title: Kyiv residents face attacks with fewer defenses overhead
item.description: Another overnight attack killed at least 17 people in and around Kyiv. The strikes come as Ukraine faces a growing shortage of the interceptor missiles used to defend the capital.
item.content:encoded: Another overnight attack killed at least 17 people in and around Kyiv. The strikes come as Ukraine faces a growing shortage of the interceptor missiles used to defend the capital.
item.dc:creator: Ailsa Chang

item.title: Myanmar's conflict tops 100,000 dead as junta benefits from world's inattention
item.description: A 2021 military coup plunged Myanmar into a brutal civil war, ousting Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government. For years, the world isolated the junta. That isolation is breaking down.
item.content:encoded: A 2021 military coup plunged Myanmar into a brutal civil war, ousting Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government. For years, the world isolated the junta. That isolation is breaking down.
item.dc:creator: Michael Sullivan

item.title: Israel is facing a shortage of army reservists
item.description: Israel is facing a substantial shortage in troop numbers as reservists, exhausted from war, are failing to turn up for duty. Experts say Israel's multiple war fronts are putting a huge mental, political, and financial strain on reservists.
item.content:encoded: Israel is facing a substantial shortage in troop numbers as reservists, exhausted from war, are failing to turn up for duty. Experts say Israel's multiple war fronts are putting a huge mental, political, and financial strain on reservists.
item.dc:creator: Emily Feng

item.title: Pakistan's ruling party leads in Kashmir vote despite boycott call by banned group
item.description: Candidates backed by twice-elected former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League-N party have won 24 of the 34 seats decided in the first two phases of voting, the election commission, said Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Candidates backed by twice-elected former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League-N party have won 24 of the 34 seats decided in the first two phases of voting, the election commission, said Wednesday.

(Image credit: M.D. Mughal)

item.description: A 73-year-old retired nurse's decision to learn to write Tibetan language offers a glimpse into how some embrace their language and cultural identity in Tibet.

item.title: U.S. missile stockpiles dwindle. And, FDA weighs approval of flu shots with mRNA tech
item.description: The U.S. Army's missile stockpile is dwindling and could take years to replenish. And, the Food and Drug Administration is deciding whether to approve a flu vaccine with mRNA technology.

item.description: Ukraine's depleted air defenses failed to stop any of Moscow's incoming missiles overnight.

item.title: Unrest mounts in Kashmir as Pakistani security crackdown stokes reform movement
item.description: Pakistani forces blockade Kashmir as protesters demand electoral reforms and -- increasingly -- revolution.

item.title: Ukraine's air defenses are proving to be a weak point
item.description: Ukraine's defenses have held the line on most fronts, but there's one glaring weakness -- Russian ballistic missiles. Ukraine is desperately short of U.S.-made Patriot air defense missiles needed to defend against the Russians.

item.title: The soaring demand for Patriot missiles, from the Middle East to Ukraine
item.description: The U.S. and its partners depend on Patriot interceptors to shoot down incoming ballistic missiles. But Russia and Iran are firing their weapons at rates far higher than Patriots can be produced.
